node2vec does not automatically learn the return parameter p or the in-out parameter q via end-to-end differentiable gradient descent in its original formulation. In the original node2vec method, p and q are user-specified hyperparameters that control the transition probabilities of the biased random walk: p discourages immediate backtracking, while q biases the walk toward breadth-first-search-like or depth-first-search-like exploration. These parameters are typically selected by grid search or manual tuning on a validation task, not optimized by backpropagation.

The reason end-to-end differentiable gradient descent is not used for p and q in standard node2vec is that the random-walk sampling procedure is discrete and non-differentiable with respect to the walk-transition choices. The node embeddings are learned with a skip-gram-style objective from sampled walks, but the walk-generation hyperparameters themselves are not part of a differentiable computation graph in the original algorithm.

If one wanted to learn p and q automatically, one would need a modified, differentiable relaxation of the walk policy or a reinforcement-learning-style estimator; that would be a new method beyond original node2vec, not the published algorithm itself. So the accurate answer is: original node2vec uses grid search or manual tuning for p and q, and it does not perform end-to-end differentiable learning of those parameters.
